questions.question: During handoff, an EMT uses an unfamiliar shorthand expression. The receiving clinician asks what it means. Which response best serves the purpose of medical terminology?

choices.text: State the finding clearly using words both clinicians understand
Repeat the shorthand because brevity is the primary goal
Substitute another abbreviation without checking whether it is understood
Leave the expression unexplained if it appears in the written report

questions.explanation: Medical terminology supports accurate shared understanding; speed should not take priority over clarity.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Brevity is useful only when the meaning is clear.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Changing shorthand does not establish shared understanding.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: A written expression can remain just as ambiguous as a spoken one.

sourceReferences.locator: I; VIII.A: Communication and accepted shorthand

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified
questions.diagnosticIntent: Medical terminology supports accurate shared understanding; speed should not take priority over clarity.
questions.whyNotBest: Brevity is useful only when the meaning is clear.
questions.keyDistinction: Medical terminology supports accurate shared understanding; speed should not take priority over clarity.

questions.question: Which list identifies the four components used to construct medical terms?

choices.text: Word root, prefix, suffix, combining vowel
Word root, combining vowel, acronym, symbol

questions.explanation: Roots supply the foundation; prefixes and suffixes modify meaning; combining vowels connect components.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: An abbreviation is shorthand, not the fourth word-building component.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Acronyms and symbols do not replace prefixes and suffixes.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: This omits the root and combining vowel.

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified
questions.diagnosticIntent: Roots supply the foundation; prefixes and suffixes modify meaning; combining vowels connect components.

questions.question: In nephr/o/pathy, what function does the o perform?

choices.text: It connects the root to the suffix and eases pronunciation
It changes the organ named by the root
It means disease and supplies the condition
It indicates that the term is plural

questions.explanation: The o is a combining vowel between nephr and -pathy; it does not carry the disease or organ meaning.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Nephr still identifies the kidney.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: The suffix -pathy supplies the disease meaning.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: A combining vowel is not a plural ending.

sourceReferences.locator: II.H; VII.A.2.a: Combining vowels and nephropathy

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified
questions.diagnosticIntent: The o is a combining vowel between nephr and -pathy; it does not carry the disease or organ meaning.
